title: Schur-certified two-scale semigroup budget for the intrinsic graph
question: Can the late-time IR leg of the R-414 semigroup criterion use the conservative harmonic/Schur gap from R-406, so that coarse inter-phase capacity and block-mean-zero residual coercivity are explicit inputs to the Green-trace budget?

new_perspective.principle: Replace the black-box first positive eigenvalue in the late heat bound by kappa_S=half min(kappa_coarse,kappa_residual), the R-406 harmonic-extension/Schur lower bound. Since kappa_S<=lambda_1, H(t)<=H(tau) exp(-kappa_S(t-tau)) and the late integral is bounded by H(tau)/kappa_S.
route: Rebuild the R-406 conditional graph, phase block partition, harmonic extension and Schur/residual gaps on every declared finite row.
Check the R-406 variational inequality kappa_S<=lambda_1 before using the certified gap in a semigroup envelope.
Enumerate all R-412 mixed exponent profiles and use the R-414 short-time UV power budget unchanged.
Check the late exponential envelope and Green-trace criterion with kappa_S, recording the coarse and residual gaps separately.
Keep all constants finite and rowwise; promotion requires uniform Schur coarse/residual bounds, a phase interpretation and a common Hamiltonian core.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: The Schur gap makes the phase-capacity and residual fluctuation channels visible in the same proper-time estimate. It is a finite interface toward broken-sector GNS coercivity, not a phase-selection or physical Yang--Mills mass-gap theorem.

finite_theorem.schur_gap: For the R-406 harmonic split, kappa_S=half min(kappa_coarse,kappa_residual) is a finite lower bound for the first positive intrinsic graph eigenvalue.
finite_theorem.short_time_budget: For 0<t<=tau and 0<alpha_UV<1, H(t)<=A_tau t^(-alpha_UV), with A_tau=r tau^alpha_UV+C_UV alpha_UV Gamma(alpha_UV).
finite_theorem.scope: Every implication is finite-dimensional and rowwise; kappa_S, A_tau and H(tau) are not asserted uniform in cutoff, volume, source, phase or exhaustion.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar ordering and positivity for the conservative gap budget; Schur spectra, conditional rows, heat traces, uniform limits and QFT reconstruction remain executable/open analysis.

promotion_criteria: Prove source/cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion-uniform lower bounds for the R-406 Schur coarse and residual gaps on one Hamiltonian common core.
Identify the coarse variables with a controlled phase boundary condition and transfer the certified late heat budget to the R-399 shell.
Combine the Schur-certified semigroup budget with the common-alpha and broken-sector GNS coercivity routes only after the uniform premises are established.
stop_conditions: If either Schur component collapses under a validated growing stress, retain the late budget only as a finite diagnostic and do not claim phasewise coercivity.
If the certified gap is replaced by a larger unverified value, retain the failed late inequality.
Finite Schur-certified heat positivity is not a common-core, phase-selection, GNS, physical-gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Schur-certified two-scale semigroup bridge only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap or UV coefficient, common core, phase selection, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The R-406 harmonic/Schur lower bound supplies a conservative finite IR input for the R-414 heat budget and makes the phase-capacity route explicit; it does not supply regulator-independent coercivity or a physical-sector conclusion.
